# Spinner

```tsx
import { Spinner } from "@lucasdost/design-system"
```

Serve para representar visualmente o processamento de uma operação rápida do sistema, em que a duração não importa ou não pode ser prevista.

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
<div className="flex items-center gap-10">
  {sizes.map((size) => (
    <Spinner key={size} size={size} />
  ))}
</div>
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Spinner component: Size 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 40 / 56px. Eight rounded bars, 1/12 of the size wide and 1/4 long, around the center at 45° steps, in Icon/Primary at 60% opacity. Everything scales with the size. The color follows `currentColor`, so a parent (like Button) can tint it with `text-current`.
Like the Figma .Spinner Animation partial, the bars don't rotate: each one runs `animate-spinner-bar` (styles/theme.css) one step later than the bar before it, so a 100% bar with a 90 / 80 / 70% tail moves clockwise, starting at the bottom as in Frame 2.

## Rules

- Import `Spinner` from `@lucasdost/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
